EO-010.previous_note: Linux realization: editor File > Set as Wallpaper... (Ctrl+Alt+W) renders one owned source+visible-annotation snapshot as sRGB PNG with alpha through the existing preparation worker, shows a guarded confirmation (target: desktop background / lock screen / both; optional desktop preview; the exact retained file path), then writes the PNG atomically with owner-only (0600) permissions under <XDG data>/com.xerahs.app/linux-qt/wallpapers/ and passes it as a file descriptor to org.freedesktop.portal.Wallpaper SetWallpaperFile (options set-on, show-preview) using the same Request/Response handling as the Screenshot portal (unique-owner subscription before the call, early-response buffering, Close on abandonment). The portal has no per-display selection, so the dialog states that the desktop applies the image to all displays with its own layout; no per-monitor backend is invented. Typed results: succeeded (file retained and path shown in status/signal), cancelled (dialog cancel writes no file and makes no portal call; portal response 1; cancel while waiting closes the Request and keeps/discloses the file because the desktop may already have applied it) and failed with stable codes wallpaper-render-failed, wallpaper-annotation-unsupported, wallpaper-encode-failed, wallpaper-storage-failed, wallpaper-permission-denied, wallpaper-service-unavailable, wallpaper-failed, wallpaper-confirmation-failed. A file the portal definitively did not use (cancel/failure/denied) is removed. Document, history, dirty state and viewport are unchanged; editor destruction during render or during the portal request is safe. Tested on a private session bus with a fake Wallpaper portal. Remaining: product-owner decision whether the portal target choice (background/lock screen/both, all displays) satisfies the 'target display/layout choice' wording as an Equivalent disposition (per-display and fill/fit layout selection are not offered by the portal), real desktop-portal qualification (GNOME/KDE/Hyprland backends), file retention/cleanup policy for old wallpaper files, and accessibility qualification.
